newsitem.title: SWEDEN: U.S. figures lift long Swedish bond yields higher.
newsitem.headline: U.S. figures lift long Swedish bond yields higher.

text.p: Long Swedish bond yields ended higher on Tuesday, lifted by U.S. statistics, while the crown was flat against the mark.

Market players also sold long bond yields and turned to shorter yields in a bout of profit-taking along with some pessimism, dealers said. * Six-month T-bill rate rises one basis point to 4.15 pct. * Ten-year bond yield jumps seven basis points to 6.84 pct. * Crown flat at 4.4790 to mark vs 4.4780 late on Monday.
Long Swedish bond yields ended higher on Tuesday, lifted by U.S. statistics, while the crown was flat against the mark.
"Yields did not have the strength to fall despite strong U.S. CPI figures," a trader said. "Then less favourable U.S. figures fuelled negative trends."
Figures showed U.S. industrial production rising more than expected and a high capacity utilisation.
But profit taking and pessimism also took their toll on long Swedish bond yields with market players turning from the long end of the market.
"There has been somewhat a portfolio change with players buying shorter bond yields for long yields," a trader said.
The six-month T-bill rate rose one basis point to 4.15 percent and the ten-year bond yield jumped seven basis points to 6.84 percent.
The crown recovered morning losses to trade at 4.4790 against the mark, little changed from 4.4780 late on Monday.
"We were up at 4.51 crowns against the mark during the night and I was told that some German banks bought marks for crowns," one dealer said.
